contentHtml:
KENYA— The Karen Hospital has successfully performed a transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in Kenya, expanding access to minimally invasive treatment for patients with aortic valve disease without the need for open-heart surgery.

The procedure involves inserting a replacement valve through a catheter, usually via a blood vessel, to treat a narrowed aortic valve that restricts blood flow from the heart.

TAVI offers an alternative to conventional surgical valve replacement for eligible patients, particularly those who may face greater risks from open-heart surgery.

Advancing minimally invasive cardiac care

Unlike traditional valve replacement surgery, which generally requires opening the chest, TAVI allows clinicians to implant a replacement valve through a less invasive approach.

Eligible patients may benefit from shorter hospital stays and faster recovery, although outcomes depend on individual health conditions and procedural factors.

The Karen Hospital credited Dr. AK Gikonyo, Dr. Prem, Dr. Shrikant and the wider clinical team for delivering the procedure.

 The hospital did not disclose the patient’s condition, the date of the intervention or further clinical details.

Implications for Kenya’s cardiac care sector

The introduction of advanced catheter-based procedures reflects the growing role of specialised cardiac services in managing structural heart disease.

Expanding local access to interventions such as TAVI could reduce the need for some patients to seek treatment abroad, while strengthening the capabilities of Kenyan cardiac teams.

However, wider adoption depends on access to specialised cardiologists, imaging technology, catheterisation laboratories, trained support staff and the devices required for valve implantation

 Treatment costs and the availability of appropriate patient assessment and follow-up care also influence access.

The Karen Hospital said it continues to expand its cardiac treatment capabilities, positioning minimally invasive interventions as part of its approach to providing advanced heart care in Kenya.
